note.question: When should an e-commerce marketplace place its private label in the sponsored top slot rather than auction that slot to third-party sellers, and how does this choice affect prices, platform revenue, sellers, and consumers?
note.overview: The paper explicitly develops a sequential game among a marketplace, two strategic third-party sellers, and consumers. Platform configuration, seller participation, simultaneous prices and auction bids, ad-slot allocation, and purchases are all endogenous equilibrium objects.

models.name: Self-Preferencing in E-Commerce Marketplaces model
models.summary: The paper explicitly develops a sequential game among a marketplace, two strategic third-party sellers, and consumers. Platform configuration, seller participation, simultaneous prices and auction bids, ad-slot allocation, and purchases are all endogenous equilibrium objects.
objects: An e-commerce platform that may sell a private label
Consumers with horizontally differentiated product preferences
inputs: The platform publicly commits to marketplace configuration
Prices and the realized product ranking are observed
The distribution of consumer locations and consideration sets is common knowledge
Each seller has an exogenous outside-option profit pi_0 and anticipates equilibrium demand, prices, and bids
decisions: The platform chooses commission, private-label entry, sponsored-slot availability, and whether to concede or contest the slot
Third-party sellers choose whether to participate
The platform/private label and third-party sellers choose product prices
Consumers choose among products in their consideration sets or the outside option
assumptions: The platform is a monopoly marketplace hosting two symmetric third-party sellers and may add one private label
Products are horizontally differentiated with zero marginal cost; vertical quality differences are absent in the focal model
Consumers consider at most two varieties in a Spokes demand model, and only the top position is prominent
Sponsored placement raises consideration probability alpha but does not change product valuation
The main model uses a pay-per-impression second-price auction, an exogenous commission phi, and moderate product valuation so equilibrium prices are interior and market coverage can change

components.label: Backward-induction platform-configuration equilibrium with simultaneous pricing and locally envy-free auction bidding
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Backward-induction platform-configuration equilibrium with simultaneous pricing and locally envy-free auction bidding. The paper solves four marketplace subgames by backward induction. Sellers' prices are mutual best responses, bids satisfy a locally envy-free second-price auction selection, and the authors verify joint price-bid deviations for the global equilibrium. The platform then compares equilibrium revenue across benchmark, advertising, private-label, concede, and contest cases.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: At T=0 the platform sets commission, decides whether to introduce a private label and sponsored slot, and if both exist whether to concede the slot or contest it for the private label. At T=1 each third-party seller chooses participation relative to its outside option. At T=2 participating sellers and the private label simultaneously set prices, and sellers submit ad-auction bids. At T=3 the second-price auction outcome is realized.
